direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is a tale of two parts: the found-footage sequences are well done and feel similar to the web series in adding a creepypasta feel, and the rest of the movie, while it does do a good job in building the world and creating suspenseful moments, feels more like a traditional Hollywood horror movie that strays from what made the IP so creepy; The direction on a microscale is not that good because they tried to make this movie a character-driven story, when that is not what the 'Backrooms' is about at all considering that the mystique adds to the horror; It is pretty obvious this movie was directed by a 20-year-old because the microscale elements definitely show a lack of experience, but it is definitely a good launchpad for a future director; Storytelling is not great because they try to create this character-driven story that just does not work considering the mystique of the 'Backrooms' IP is what makes it so compelling; Tension is built very well, especially in the found-footage sequences, as it helps create this creepy atmosphere that makes you crawl into your seat as you wait for something to happen

performance.comments: Shows his experience as an actor as he feels like a lightning rod for which the energy of the room he's in absorbs, making all the performances flow throuh him; despite characters being able to flow through him, the chemistry in his scenes are not the best mainly because there is nothing to really work with

This role honestly doens't feel like it accentuates her talents as an actress because she's asked to be this scared, loud screem-queen when she is more of a grounded, subtle actress; this mismatch in style comes out because she's asked to be loud and scream right before the climax, but it just comes off as flat

cast.comments: There really isn't that much of a cast outside of the main two, but there really isn't that much chemistry in the cast as a whole

story.comments: The concept is a huge issue for this movie because they tried to make this character-driven story about the 'Backrooms' when the IP is all about the mystery and ominous nature of the setting; The plot structure is not the best as the movie spends way too much time on exposition and character building in the first half, so it does not leave enough time for the horror elements to thrive; Character writing is very weak as they tried to make this character-driven story, but you do not really care about any of these characters because they are not written very well and do not match what the IP is about

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is pretty generic; The symbolism is present, but it kind of hurts this movie because it is trying to be something that the 'Backrooms' isn't; The foreshadowing is present and does a decent job in building the story

score.comments: The score helps build suspense and tension that helps amplify the horror elements as you are crawling into your seat waiting for something to happen

cinematography.comments: I really enjoyed the found-footage sequences because that style is what the 'Backrooms' really is; The rest of the cinematography really threw me off because they used crystal-clear digital cameras, but since the movie is set in 1990, my concept of time was thrown off; The camera work in the digital sequences was good though as it helped build the vast nature of the Backrooms and helped make you feel lost in the world

editing.comments: The editing felt standard; But I did enjoy the editing in the found-footage sequences and in the climax

sound.comments: The sound was used well to help build suspense and tension in the horror sequences

visual_effects.comments: Given the budget, I think it does a good job, but I would have really liked for them to not show the monster because it really took out the mystique and fear that the IP tried to build with its web series; It feels very different from the creepypasta nature of the web series because that was made entirely in Blender while this looks very Hollywood

production_design.comments: The sets genuinely are amazing as they help transport you into the Backrooms and the creepy, unsettling world they are in

makeup.comments: The makeup obviously looked fake, which added to the unsettling nature of the film, but also made it feel tacky

review.pacing: Pacing is a big problem for this movie because it spends way too much time on character building and exposition, which really makes the scary elements feel more like an afterthought and less impactful
review.climax: The climax is executed well, but it feels like a strong departure from what made the 'Backrooms' so creepy and unsettling in the first place, opting for a more action-oriented Hollywood climax rather than a suspenseful, creepypasta one
review.tone: The tone is a mix because the found-footage sequences feel closer to the original web series, but the rest of the movie feels like a traditional Hollywood horror movie that tries to be character-driven but falls flat
review.overall: Overall, 'Backrooms' is an example of how an IP does not match the medium, as the movie tries to build a character-driven story that tries to explain the world, but the 'Backrooms' IP is all about the mystique and unsettling nature of the unknown; This juxtaposition is clear in the cinematography as the found-footage sequences are well executed and feel true to the IP, but the crystal-clear, digital sequences feel like a traditional Hollywood movie that does not match the source material; despite its flaws, 'Backrooms' is still a decent horror movie that will satisfy your scare cravings, even though it does fall flat in trying to be something that the source material isn't
